s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of skin and muscle symptoms following immunotherapy
salient_findings: Prominent erythema at nailfolds with dilated capillary loops
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Diagnosed with stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma
Metastases in liver, lungs, and peritoneum
Received ipilimumab treatment
Developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab
Experienced initial improvement and later disease recurrence
Received a second course of ipilimumab 14 months later
Symptoms recurred and worsened after second course of ipilimumab
Physical findings include photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption
Elevated creatine kinase levels (1088 U/L and 1854 U/L)
Aldolase level: 23.0 U/L
C-reactive protein level: 28.6 mg/L
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:640 with speckled pattern
Jo-1 antibody: negative
MRI showed mild short TI inversion recovery hyperintensity of bilateral vastus lateralis and rectus femoris muscles
Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers

shortlist.why_kept: Elevated creatine kinase levels and muscle weakness

raw.rationale: The patient developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab treatment, and symptoms recurred and worsened after a second course of ipilimumab, suggesting a temporal relationship between ipilimumab treatment and the development of myositis

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While the patient has skin symptoms consistent with dermatomyositis, the temporal relationship with ipilimumab treatment and the absence of inflammatory myositis on biopsy suggest ipilimumab-induced myositis is a more likely diagnosis

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The patient's muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers without evidence of inflammatory myositis, which is not typical of polymyositis

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While the patient has melanoma, the temporal relationship between ipilimumab treatment and the development of myositis suggests that the myositis is more likely related to the treatment rather than the underlying cancer

rejected.label: Necrotizing autoimmune myopathy
rejected.why: The patient's muscle biopsy did not show evidence of necrotizing autoimmune myopathy

rejected.label: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy
rejected.why: The patient's muscle biopsy did not show evidence of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy

rejected.label: Melanoma-associated myositis
rejected.why: The temporal relationship between ipilimumab treatment and the development of myositis suggests that the myositis is more likely related to the treatment rather than the underlying cancer

rejected.label: PD-1 inhibitor-associated myositis
rejected.why: Ipilimumab is a CTLA-4 inhibitor, not a PD-1 inhibitor, making this diagnosis less likely
